about: Every day of 2026 on which the FSSP ordo of the engine (src/ordo.ts with data/ordos/fssp.json, and the United States and FSSP layers) differs from the FSSP seminary's page (fsspolgs.org/liturgical-calendar, read 2026-11-09): the first printed row against the ordo's first Mass, its class and commemorations, and every other row against the Masses the ordo lists. The page is not in this repository; set FSSP_PAGE to a saved copy to re-check. On the other 342 days the first row is the ordo's first Mass and every row is one the ordo lists.

groups.group: the page prints first another Mass the ordo offers
groups.why: The page puts first a Mass the engine also lists for the day, but no rule of data/ordos/fssp.json does so: on other days of the same kind the page prints the Mass of the day first. The Mass of a commemorated saint first on 14 February, 17 April and 24 September, but second on every other 4th class day with a commemoration (19 January, 3 February, 20 June and others); the Rogation Mass first on Monday 11 May, second on 25 April, 12 and 13 May; a Mass for certain places first on 27 June and 27 November, second on 8 May, 6 July, 1 and 3 August, 5 November. On 17 April and 24 September the page prints no other row.

groups.group: the page offers a Mass the rubrics do not permit that day
groups.why: On a day the United States keeps a 3rd class feast, the page also prints the Masses of the universal calendar's day. The Mass of a commemoration is permitted only on a 4th class day (no. 303b): St. Telesphorus on 5 January and St. Gorgonius on 9 September are commemorated on a 3rd class feast. A feria's Mass is not a festive Mass in the broad sense (no. 302): the feria of 9 September and the Advent feria of 12 December are impeded by a 3rd class feast.

groups.group: the calendar differs from the page
groups.why: The first Mass is the day's own and the difference is in the calendar, reviewed in test/fixtures/fssp-2026-differences.json: the page differs from the rubrics (1 and 11 January, 28 June, 8 September, 16 and 17 December), the Fraternity's own feast is not on the page (23 February), commemorations in another order (27 March, 1 September, 21 October, 4 December), and a Mass for certain places commemorated in the row of the day (8 May, 4 July, 6 July). On 4 July the first row is the votive Mass of the Immaculate Heart, as the engine has it, with the Mass for certain places commemorated.
